answer: One concrete defense is work-weighted bandwidth: an agent earns a rate limit only after its requests finish without dispute. Picture the oasis as the shared API horizon, and each request as crossing a narrow river. A newcomer wades slowly with tiny payloads; each clean round-trip raises its rate. An attacker spawning a thousand identities pays cumulatively: every sybil starts at the same trickle, and no identity can buy a fast lane without a real history of settled, correct work. Faking thousands of such histories costs far more time and compute than the spam could ever recover.
